BiblicalUsage: lᵉbab means the heart, and it is one of those words that quietly holds a whole theme together. In Daniel 5:20, "But when his heart was lifted up"; and in Daniel 5:22, "hast not humbled thine heart". In Daniel 7:4, "and a man's heart was given to it."; and in Daniel 4:16, "and let a beast's heart be given unto him".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the heart is the throne God deposes — Nebuchadnezzar's heart was lifted up in pride, and his heart was made like a beast's. I hold that Daniel's warning to Belshazzar still stands: a heart that will not humble itself will be humbled. My position is that I want God to change my heart before pride changes it for me.
